name: Palak Paneer

ingredients.name: Spinach (palak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium bunch; about 4 packed cups of leaves

ingredients.name: Ice cubes + cold water (for chilling spinach)

equipment: Saucepan or patila (1.5–2 litre) for blanching
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp ≈ 5 ml)

steps.title: Pick the spinach
steps.text: Pull 150 g spinach leaves off the bunch, keeping only the thin tender stems. Throw away thick stalks and yellow or damaged leaves.
steps.tip: thick, mature stalks are the main cause of a bitter gravy.
steps.visualCue: a pile of whole green leaves with only short, thin stems
steps.cameraCheck: the picked leaves next to the discarded stalks
steps.videoShot: hand snapping leaves off thick stems

steps.title: Wash the spinach
steps.text: Put the leaves in a big bowl of water, swish, lift them out, and repeat with fresh water 2–3 times.
steps.visualCue: no grit at the bottom of the bowl on the last wash
steps.cameraCheck: clean water at the bottom of the bowl
steps.videoShot: leaves lifted out of the water by hand

steps.title: Boil water
steps.text: Put 750 ml (3 cups) water in the saucepan on high heat.
steps.visualCue: big, rolling bubbles
steps.cameraCheck: the saucepan at a rolling boil
steps.videoShot: water bubbling hard

steps.title: Make the ice bath
steps.text: Fill a bowl with 500 ml cold water and 6–8 ice cubes.
steps.visualCue: ice floating in the water
steps.videoShot: ice cubes dropped into water

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces
steps.videoShot: knife chopping onion finely

steps.title: Chop tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 60 g (1 small) tomato.
steps.visualCue: small juicy pieces
steps.videoShot: tomato diced on the board

steps.title: Prep ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Peel and roughly chop 5 g ginger and 2 garlic cloves. Slit 1 green chilli and remove the stem.
steps.visualCue: three small heaps
steps.cameraCheck: ginger, garlic and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: garlic cloves being peeled and chopped

steps.title: Cube and soak paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes and cover with warm (not boiling) water.
steps.visualCue: even cubes submerged in water
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of paneer cubes in water
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes slid into warm water

steps.title: Blanch the spinach
steps.text: Push the spinach leaves into the boiling water with a spoon so they are all under.
steps.tip: take them out as soon as they are limp. Longer turns them dull olive and bitter.
steps.visualCue: leaves are limp and bright, vivid green; stems bend easily
steps.cameraCheck: the pot of bright-green wilted leaves
steps.videoShot: leaves sinking and wilting in boiling water

steps.title: Chill the spinach
steps.text: Lift the spinach out with a slotted spoon (or drain) and drop it straight into the ice water.
steps.visualCue: leaves are cold to the touch and stay bright green
steps.cameraCheck: green leaves in the ice bowl
steps.videoShot: steaming leaves plunged into ice water

steps.title: Squeeze the spinach
steps.text: Lift the leaves out and gently squeeze out the extra water with your hands.
steps.visualCue: a compact green ball, not dripping
steps.cameraCheck: the squeezed spinach ball in your palm
steps.videoShot: hands pressing water from the spinach

steps.title: Blend the purée
steps.text: Put the spinach, ginger, garlic and green chilli in the small mixer jar with 2 tbsp of the ice water and blend until smooth.
steps.tip: blend in short bursts so the motor heat doesn't dull the colour.
steps.visualCue: thick, smooth, bright-green purée with only tiny flecks
steps.videoShot: green purée being scraped down the jar

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: oil swirling in the kadai

steps.title: Temper cumin
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.visualCue: seeds sizzle and turn a shade darker; nutty smell
steps.videoShot: cumin crackling in oil

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: soft and light golden at the edges
steps.videoShot: onion sizzling as it's stirred

steps.title: Add tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and a pinch of the salt and stir.
steps.visualCue: tomato turns mushy and the mix looks jammy
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, pressing tomato with the spatula
steps.videoShot: spatula squashing soft tomato

steps.title: Add spice powders
steps.text: Lower the heat. Add the pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ½ tsp coriander powder and stir.
steps.tip: if it starts sticking, add 1 tbsp water instead of more oil.
steps.visualCue: masala turns reddish and smells toasty, not burnt
steps.videoShot: spices sprinkled and stirred in

steps.title: Add spinach purée
steps.text: Pour in the spinach purée and stir it into the masala.
steps.visualCue: evenly green gravy with flecks of onion
steps.videoShot: green purée poured into the masala

steps.title: Loosen with water
steps.text: Add 60 ml (¼ cup) water and the rest of the salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: gravy flows slowly off the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: the spatula lifted out of the gravy
steps.videoShot: gravy dripping off the spatula

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Simmer on low, partly covered (it splutters).
steps.tip: don't cook longer than about 4 minutes, or the colour goes dull.
steps.visualCue: gentle bubbles; still bright green, slightly thicker
steps.videoShot: green gravy bubbling lazily

steps.title: Add paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Fold gently.
steps.visualCue: every cube coated in green gravy
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes folded into the gravy

steps.title: Simmer paneer
steps.text: Simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: paneer is warmed through and soft
steps.videoShot: slow bubbles around white paneer cubes

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: aroma becomes noticeably "restaurant-like"
steps.videoShot: kasuri methi crushed between palms

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed
steps.videoShot: garam masala sprinkled over

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Swirl in 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh cream.
steps.tip: adding cream with the heat off stops it splitting.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a lighter, glossy green
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through green gravy

steps.title: Taste and plate
steps.text: Taste; add ½ tsp lemon juice if it tastes flat (optional). Spoon into a bowl, with a small swirl of cream on top if you like.
steps.visualCue: bright-green curry with white paneer cubes
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl

reasons: A big portion of leafy greens (150 g spinach) gives fibre, folate, vitamin A/K and some iron, and paneer adds ~18 g of protein and plenty of calcium. Nothing is fried and there's no added sugar. Fat is still fairly high (~35 g, much of it saturated from paneer and cream). Restaurant versions often use more cream and butter, fry the paneer, and add more salt.

researchRating.basis: one of the most-loved North Indian vegetarian curries, with very high recipe ratings from large numbers of home cooks. Recurring complaints are a bitter or "metallic" taste and dull brown-green colour when the spinach is overcooked, mature, or reheated.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 1–2 days (est.); the colour dulls and the spinach taste gets stronger with each day. Freezer: the spinach gravy alone (without paneer and cream) freezes for up to 1 month (est.); add fresh paneer when reheating. Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 1–2 tbsp water, stirring, just until hot. Don't boil or reheat more than once: repeated heating makes it more bitter and brown.
leftoverRemix: Palak paneer stuffed paratha. Cook the leftover curry down until thick and dry, mash the paneer into it, cool, then stuff into atta dough and roll out into parathas. Cook on a tawa with a few drops of oil and serve with curd.
burnOff: about 6.7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 9.4 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).
